Tell the browser what to do before it discovers resources itself

The browser's main resource discovery happens as it parses HTML — a serial process. Resource hints allow you to express intent before discovery: "I'll need this font", "I'll need a connection to this CDN", "fetch this script in the background". These sit in <head> and execute early, parallelising work the browser would otherwise do sequentially.

dns-prefetch — Resolves DNS for a hostname early (free, ~20ms saved). Use for all third-party origins you'll use soon: analytics, fonts, CDN.
preconnect — DNS + TCP + TLS in advance (~80ms saved). More expensive than dns-prefetch. Use for critical third-party connections (font CDN, API host).
preload — Fetch a resource at HIGH priority before it's discovered. For: LCP hero image, critical fonts, render-blocking CSS. MUST use for resources critical for initial render.
prefetch — Fetch at IDLE priority for future navigation. For: likely next page JS bundles. Browser may ignore if bandwidth-constrained.
prerender — Full background render of next page (Chrome 108+). For: predictable next steps (add-to-cart →checkout). Very high cost, use sparingly.
fetchpriority — Priority Hints API. Adjust browser default priority: high/low/auto. Use high on LCP image, low on below-fold images.

Resource hint selection guide

HintCostPriorityTimingUse when
dns-prefetchVery low (DNS only)LowImmediateAny 3rd-party origin you'll call
preconnectMedium (TCP+TLS)MediumImmediateOrigins needed within 3s of load
preloadHigh (full fetch)HighImmediateCritical fonts, LCP image, key CSS
prefetchLow (idle)LowestAfter load eventNext page JS, predictable navigation
prerenderVery high (full page)SpeculativeBackgroundHigh-confidence next page only
fetchpriority=highChanges order, not costBoostOn element renderLCP image, critical <script>
fetchpriority=lowChanges order, not costReduceOn element renderBelow-fold images, non-critical assets

Complete resource hints implementation

<!-- In <head> — order matters, these run early -->

<!-- 1. Preconnect: establishes DNS + TCP + TLS early -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.example.com">

<!-- 2. DNS prefetch for less critical third-party origins -->
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://www.googletagmanager.com">
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://static.hotjar.com">

<!-- 3. Preload: fetch critical resources ASAP -->
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="/images/hero.avif"
  type="image/avif" fetchpriority="high">
<link rel="preload" as="font" href="/fonts/inter-var.woff2"
  type="font/woff2" crossorigin>

<!-- 4. Priority Hints on key elements -->
<img src="hero.avif" fetchpriority="high" alt="Hero">   <!-- LCP -->
<img src="below-fold.webp" fetchpriority="low" loading="lazy" alt="Secondary">

<!-- 5. Prefetch next page's JS chunks -->
<link rel="prefetch" href="/_next/static/chunks/checkout.js">

// Dynamic prefetch based on user intent (hover on link)
const observer = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
  entries.filter(e => e.isIntersecting).forEach(e => {
    const href = e.target.getAttribute('href');
    if (href) prefetchRoute(href);
  });
});
document.querySelectorAll('a[data-prefetch]').forEach(el => observer.observe(el));
